identity.name: ASHAPURA MINECHEM LTD
identity.industry: Mining & Bulk Minerals — Bauxite (Guinea export) + Industrial/Specialty Minerals (Bentonite, adsorbents, ceramics); aluminium-feedstock value chain

summary.oneLiner: Ashapura's Guinea bauxite export engine drove an all-time-best year (FY26 consol revenue INR 5,237 cr, +91% YoY; Q4 revenue INR 1,969 cr, +105% QoQ on volume ramp to ~8 Mt FY26 from 3.5 Mt) but Q4 EBITDA/ton collapsed to ~$5.9 (margins ~14%→~7%) as bauxite prices corrected and ocean freight/fuel spiked on the war/geopolitics. The bull case is a near-term Guinea **bauxite quota system** (expected within a month) that should curb 70-80 Mt mega-miners, cut export supply ~20-25%, lift net bauxite prices and ease freight — disproportionately benefiting small concession-holders like Ashapura, whose own concessions carry no refinery/value-add obligation.

> Distortion to watch: headline FY26 growth is overwhelmingly a Guinea bauxite **volume** story (3.5→8 Mt); the per-ton EBITDA already rolled over hard in Q4 ($5.9). Q1 FY27 guided similar-to-slightly-worse before quota relief.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume:** Guinea bauxite ~10-12 Mt in FY27 (vs 8 Mt FY26); 15 Mt target reaffirmed for **FY27-28** (next-next year); port capacity build to 27 Mt over medium term.
- **Revenue:** Guinea ~$700m+ turnover FY27 (at ~$70/t, 10-12 Mt). India: growth similar to / better than FY26.
- **Margin:** Q1 FY27 EBITDA similar to or slightly worse than Q4 (elevated fuel/freight, war); full-year FY27 EBITDA expected better than Q4 on a yearly basis once quota lands. Mgmt believes "close to bottom of the cycle." Targeting return toward FY25-type ~10-10.5% margin by year-end (aspirational, not committed).
- **Quota system (key swing factor):** Guinea bauxite export quota expected to be **announced within ~a month**; expected to curb large miners, reduce supply ~20-25%, improve net bauxite price (bauxite minus freight) and ease freight.
- **Capex:** India ~INR 150 cr next year across divisions (plant upgrades + new value-added products). Guinea iron-ore/bauxite beneficiation plants — exploring **BOT / vendor-funded / partner** models to keep off balance sheet (nothing finalized).
- **Iron ore (Guinea):** commissioning slower than expected; meaningful contribution "couple of years"; beneficiation plant for iron ore in ~3-4 quarters; sizing >1.5 Mt; targeting 60%+ Fe export grade from 40-50% ROM; pellet plant possible later (not focus).
- **Bauxite washing plant:** 20,000 tpd capacity to upgrade sub-marketable bauxite to marketable grade.
order book & pipeline:
Not an order-book business (commodity export + industrial minerals). Demand visibility instead:
- Long-standing 20+ yr customer relationships in China; large Chinese refineries each consume 25-30 Mt/yr; customers pulling forward shipments ahead of expected quota-driven price rise.
- 7 new bentonite leases granted this quarter (India resource replenishment / backward integration).
- Guinea concessions: no new licenses to be issued by govt for 3-5 yrs → scarcity value for existing holders.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Guinea bauxite (FY26 ~INR 4,200 cr rev, ~INR 561 cr EBITDA — largest):** 8 Mt exported FY26. Ashapura is a small ~4% player of ~200 Mt Guinea exports (a "drop in the ocean"), self-described price-taker. Ports: Boffa (~5→~10 Mt, expansion near-complete) + GSM (~6 Mt, +50-60% by FY27-28); roads/infra already in place. Long-term shipping-line freight contracts cushioned the freight spike. Guinea has near-zero income tax for Ashapura for at least next 1-2 yrs (investment recovery).
- **India — Bentonite & Allied / White Performance Minerals (FY26 ~INR 998 cr rev, ~INR 112 cr EBITDA):** ~35% India bentonite market share; >40% of India's bentonite exports (largest exporter). Main app = iron-ore pelletizing; developing value-added grades for oil & gas, foundry, paints, paper, steel (import-substitution).
- **Specialty Adsorbent Solutions (50% JV Ashapura Perfoclay):** hit by sharp rise in sulfuric acid (key RM).
- **Advanced Ceramic Materials (Orient Ceratech stake):** encouraging growth YoY — the one India bright spot.
- **Iron ore (Guinea, new):** ~300 sq km mines, few hundred Mt reserves, 40-50% Fe ROM, beneficiable to 60%+; in commissioning; mining-only economics so single-digit margins.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Guinea iron-ore monetization (beneficiation, possibly pellets later) — multi-year optionality.
- Bauxite washing plant (20k tpd) to convert currently sub-marketable bauxite into saleable product (resource yield uplift).
- India value-added minerals (oil & gas / foundry / paints / steel) — slower-burn compounding "moats."
- Exploring other African geographies for bauxite (delegations sent; very early).
- 27 Mt port capacity build = headroom well beyond current volumes.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 EBITDA/ton crushed to ~$5.9 by: (1) bauxite price correction (CIF China fell to ~$60 Jan-Mar); (2) ocean freight spike (war/Middle East routes — Guinea→China less hit but global freight repriced); (3) higher fuel; (4) Guinea govt duty/tax tied to LME aluminium (which rose). Recent price recovery to ~$68-69 is "almost entirely freight," hence conservative near-term margin view.
- India: fuel/logistics inflation + sulfuric-acid cost + adverse mix (more low-margin product).
- Levers: beneficiation/washing plants to lower delivered cost; quota-driven freight easing; aluminium at ~$3,600 heading toward ~$4,000 supports bauxite demand.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- India ~INR 150 cr FY27 (plants + new products).
- Guinea port expansions (Boffa near-done; GSM by FY27-28) toward 27 Mt.
- Beneficiation plants (bauxite washing 20k tpd; iron-ore beneficiation >1.5 Mt) — seeking off-BS / BOT / partner funding.
- Slippage risk: iron-ore commissioning already behind; quota timing & freight are external.
capital allocation:
- 100% dividend recommended FY26.
- Explicit focus on NOT raising debt; prefers BOT/vendor-funded models for beneficiation capex; WC will rise with volume but mgmt targets medium-term debt reduction.
- Strong cash generation acknowledged by analysts.
risks & watch-items:
- **Quota uncertainty:** entire bull case hinges on a quota whose size/allocation is unknown; could disappoint. Also could (medium-term, low odds now) extend value-add/refinery obligations to all miners — mgmt says Ashapura's concessions are exempt.
- **Freight/fuel volatility** (war, vessel availability) — the single biggest threat to volume/margin; the only scenario mgmt would slow ramp.
- **Bauxite price** is a commodity Ashapura cannot control (4% share, price-taker).
- **Geopolitical/Guinea sovereign risk**; duty/tax linked to LME aluminium.
- **Iron-ore execution slippage** (commissioning delays, grade realization).
- **India margins** structurally pressured (sulfuric acid, fuel, mix).
management quality / tone: Promoter-led, candid and detailed; Manan Shah fielded almost all Q&A with clear, hedged answers (repeatedly flagged "speculative"). Openly owned the EBITDA/ton collapse and Q1 weakness rather than spinning it. Strategy coherent: ride Guinea scarcity, keep capex off balance sheet, compound India value-add. Slightly promotional on multi-year iron-ore/value-add optionality but appropriately caveated on timing. Self-aware on price-taker status. Notable correction: clarified Guinea (Africa) vs Guyana (S. America) for an analyst.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline 91% growth masks a margin top: EBITDA/ton already fell to $5.9 in Q4 — FY27 is a margin-recovery story, not a growth-acceleration story, and depends almost entirely on an external policy event (the quota).
- A bauxite **export quota** is counter-intuitively bullish for the small player: it caps the 70-80 Mt mega-miners and redistributes/curbs supply, lifting net price and easing freight — Ashapura positioned as a beneficiary, not a victim, of supply restriction.
- Concession quality is a hidden moat: unlike Chinese majors, Ashapura's Guinea concessions carry **no refinery/value-add obligation** and govt won't issue new licenses for 3-5 yrs → scarcity rent.
- The "$700m Guinea turnover" FY27 frame at ~$70/t implies the volume ramp continues even as per-ton economics stay soft near-term.
- India is a slow compounder behind the Guinea cash machine — Orient Ceratech (ceramics) the only India unit that grew; adsorbents JV hurt by sulfuric acid.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

identity.name: ASHAPURA MINECHEM LTD
identity.industry: Mining & Bulk Minerals — Bauxite (Guinea export) + Industrial/Specialty Minerals (Bentonite, adsorbents, ceramics); aluminium-feedstock value chain

hero.oneLiner: Ashapura's Guinea bauxite export engine drove an all-time-best year (FY26 consol revenue INR 5,237 cr, +91% YoY; Q4 revenue INR 1,969 cr, +105% QoQ on volume ramp to ~8 Mt FY26 from 3.5 Mt) but Q4 EBITDA/ton collapsed to ~$5.9 (margins ~14%→~7%) as bauxite prices corrected and ocean freight/fuel spiked on the war/geopolitics. The bull case is a near-term Guinea **bauxite quota system** (expected within a month) that should curb 70-80 Mt mega-miners, cut export supply ~20-25%, lift net bauxite prices and ease freight — disproportionately benefiting small concession-holders like Ashapura, whose own concessions carry no refinery/value-add obligation.
